audits.title: A multidisciplinary audit of diabetic care using criteria mapping.
audits.standard: Criteria Map of 23 criteria (18 medical, three dietetic, one nursing); score above 75% indicates adequate care

cycle1.result: Medical compliance 78.46%, dietetic 79.17%, nursing 85.71%; mean dossier score 80.62%

audits.other_findings: Documentation of services, especially patient education, needed to be more complete.
audits.citation: White L, Currie LJ, Jarvis KE. A multidisciplinary audit of diabetic care using criteria mapping. J Can Diet Assoc. 1984;45(3):255-261. PMID: 10267393.

audits.title: Improving the Clinical Interpretability of Inpatient Blood Glucose Monitoring Through a Standardized Documentation Chart: A Quality Improvement Study at a Tertiary Public Hospital in the Caribbean.
audits.standard: Predefined documentation standards for inpatient blood glucose monitoring
audits.setting: Adult medical inpatients, tertiary public hospital (University of the West Indies, Kingston)

cycle1.result: Clinically interpretable charts 10/25 (40%); meal-related timing 9/25 (36%); insulin adjacent to glucose 14/25 (56%); overall compliance 11/25 (44%); incomplete charts 8/25 (32%).

audits.intervention: Redesigned timing-based paper diabetes monitoring chart implemented hospital-wide with staff education.

cycle2.result: Clinically interpretable 23/25 (92%, p < 0.001); meal-related timing 23/25 (92%); insulin adjacent 24/25 (96%); overall compliance 23/25 (92%); incomplete charts 2/25 (8%, p = 0.074).

audits.other_findings: Two-cycle audit conducted over six months.
audits.citation: Lyons C. Improving the Clinical Interpretability of Inpatient Blood Glucose Monitoring Through a Standardized Documentation Chart: A Quality Improvement Study at a Tertiary Public Hospital in the Caribbean. Cureus. 2026;18(8):e114677. doi:10.7759/cureus.114677. PMID: 42751409.

audits.title: The Queensland Inpatient Diabetes Survey (QuIDS) 2019: the bedside audit of practice.
audits.standard: Quality of inpatient diabetes care: good diabetes days, medication errors, hospital-acquired harm, specialist review, foot and perioperative care
audits.setting: 27 public hospitals in Queensland (Queensland Inpatient Diabetes Survey)

cycle1.result: Good diabetes days 22.1 per 100 patient-days (type 1) and 40.1 (insulin-treated type 2); medication errors in 201 (32%), insulin prescribing errors in 127 (39%); 121 (14%) eligible for specialist review not reviewed.

audits.other_findings: Hypoglycaemia 24.1 episodes per 100 patient-days in type 1 diabetes; four patients with type 1 diabetes developed DKA in hospital (8%).
audits.citation: Donovan P, Eccles-Smith J, Hinton N, Cutmore C, Porter K, Abel J, et al.. The Queensland Inpatient Diabetes Survey (QuIDS) 2019: the bedside audit of practice. Med J Aust. 2021;215(3):119-124. doi:10.5694/mja2.51048. PMID: 33940660.

audits.title: Inpatient management of diabetes and hyperglycaemia: an audit of Spanish hospitals.
audits.standard: Capillary blood glucose in target 80-180 mg/dl; quality of inpatient diabetes care
audits.setting: Internal medicine departments of 53 hospitals, one-day cross-sectional audit

cycle1.result: On day 3, glucose in target pre-breakfast 792/1126 (70.3%), pre-lunch 601/1083 (55.4%), pre-dinner 591/1073 (55.0%), night 317/529 (59.9%); hypoglycaemia in 35 (0.9%); sliding scale insulin used in 352 (40.5%); recent HbA1c in 735 (61.6%).

audits.other_findings: Basal plus rapid insulin in 434 (50%); SGLT2i use increased at discharge (30.1% vs 21.6%); authors note excessive sliding scale use and insufficient HbA1c information.
audits.citation: Ena J, Carretero-Gómez J, Manuel-Casas J, Casado P, Vázquez-Rodríguez P, Martínez-García F, et al.. Inpatient management of diabetes and hyperglycaemia: an audit of Spanish hospitals. Rev Clin Esp (Barc). 2023;223(7):387-395. doi:10.1016/j.rceng.2023.04.011. PMID: 37295647.

audits.title: Improving the Timing of Acute Care Insulin Delivery.
audits.standard: Best practice: insulin within one hour of blood glucose result and bedtime insulin per order set; project goal 92%
audits.setting: 520-bed acute care teaching hospital (Pennsylvania Hospital, Philadelphia)

cycle1.result: Insulin given more than one hour after glucose results 97% of the time (3% within one hour); bedtime insulin given 37% of the time.

audits.intervention: Protocol development, education sessions and an online module for nurses and patient care technicians, and monthly adherence feedback at safety huddles and staff meetings.

cycle2.result: Bedtime insulin rose to 82% within two weeks and was sustained to May 2022; insulin within one hour rose to 64% (October-December 2019) and to a sustained level above the 92% goal two years later.

audits.citation: Cohen S, Clark RRS. Improving the Timing of Acute Care Insulin Delivery. Am J Nurs. 2024;124(2):48-54. doi:10.1097/01.naj.0001006704.88157.20. PMID: 38270423.
